name: WEMOS D1 mini (ESP8266)
summary: ESP8266 WiFi board in a 34 x 25 mm footprint. Only one ADC and a handful of usable GPIO, several of which are boot strapping pins, the constraint that defines most D1 mini projects.
notes: The D-numbers on the silkscreen are not GPIO numbers. D1 is GPIO5, D2 is GPIO4, the opposite of what you would guess. Always check the GPIO column.

Boot strapping: GPIO0 (D3) must be high at boot for normal start and low for flash mode; GPIO2 (D4) must be high; GPIO15 (D8) must be low. Pull-ups and pull-downs on those pins decide whether the board boots at all.
A0 is the only analog input and reads 0-3.2 V through an on-board divider, giving roughly 0-1 V at the chip.

GPIO16 (D0) comes off a different peripheral block: no interrupts, no PWM, no I2C, and it has a weak internal pull-down rather than a pull-up. It is the pin that wakes the chip from deep sleep when tied to RST.
I2C is done in software on the ESP8266, so SDA/SCL can be any usable GPIO; D1/D2 are only the Arduino core defaults.
Pins are 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant, though the 5V pin passes USB power straight through for peripherals.

pins.name: RST
pins.note: Tie to D0 (GPIO16) to wake from deep sleep.

pins.name: A0
pins.note: 0-3.2 V input range through an on-board divider. 10-bit.

pins.name: D0
pins.note: No interrupt, no PWM, no I2C. Internal pull-down only.

pins.name: D8
pins.note: Strapping pin: must be low at boot. Has a 10k pull-down on board.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.note: ~500 mA from the on-board regulator, minus what the radio draws in bursts.

pins.name: TX
pins.note: Shared with the USB bridge and the boot log.

pins.name: D1
pins.note: One of the two safest general-purpose pins, no strapping role.

pins.name: D3
pins.note: Strapping pin: high to boot, low for flash mode. Has a 10k pull-up; a button to GND is fine, a steady load is not.

pins.name: D4
pins.note: Strapping pin: must be high at boot. LED is active-low.

pins.name: 5V
pins.note: Straight to the micro-USB rail. Usable as a 5 V input to power the board.
